title: Low-Dose Atomic Resolution EELS Mapping at Cryogenic Temperature
content: Cryogenic cooling in the scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) is critical for the characterization of materials undergoing low temperature phase changes such as high temperature superconductors, ferroics and multiferroics, as well as an effective beam damage reduction strategy for a range of both hard and soft materials. While atomic resolution imaging and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) analysis has become widely accessible due to the commercial availability of aberration-corrected high-brightness probes, flexible scan control systems and highly efficient energy-loss spectrometers, achieving the same resolution under cryogenic conditions remains challenging for beam sensitive samples that cannot be subjected to the high probe currents (10s to 100s of pA) typically used in an analytical STEM [1].
